prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map orders the scene into four main layers: a very bright brown paper bag on the far right at ~0.3–0.5 m, a dark round tabletop with a Perrier bottle, a white disposable cup, wrapped food items, and a Reese's pack at ~0.4–0.9 m, a seated woman across the table at ~0.9–1.2 m (roughly 0.3–0.6 m behind the tabletop objects), and dark beverage coolers behind her at ~2.0–2.5 m. All tabletop items and the paper bag are within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the woman, whose folded arms rest directly on the far edge of the table just behind the cup and food container. In frame 1 the paper bag heavily occludes the right side of the table, and across frames 1 to 5 the camera wearer shifts and tilts downward and leftward as the bag retreats to the right edge and the foreground table surface approaches slightly, which simultaneously crops the top of the woman's head out of the upper frame boundary from frame 2 onward. The map makes the continuous front-to-back depth gradient across the slanted black tabletop and the exact standoff distance between the bottle, cup, and the woman's forearms much clearer than in the dark RGB image. However, the depth map is unreliable on the glass cooler doors in the background, which Collapse into a nearly uniform black void, and in frame 5 where motion blur causes the foreground bottle and paper bag silhouettes to bleed into the table.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the foreground silhouettes and tabletop layout, showing the woman seated centrally at ~0.9–1.2 m in front of the camera wearer with her torso facing forward, while a green Perrier bottle (~0.5 m away, right-center), a white cup just behind and left of the bottle (~0.6 m), and a food tray on the left (~0.7 m) sit on the round table within arm's reach of both people. It explicitly captures occlusions and partial visibility across the sequence, showing the bottle overlapping the white cup and the woman's left arm in frames 1–4, while the tall object on the right edge narrows as the camera pans left and tilts down between frames 1 and 5. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the map makes the exact pixel boundaries separating the overlapping cup, bottle, and the woman's dark sleeve against the dark tabletop immediately distinct in the middle frames, and even picks up individual bottles inside the background cooler at ~2 m. However, the class labels and masks are highly unreliable in several places: the brown paper bag at ~0.4 m on the right is misclassified as a second "person" in frames 1–4, the background beverage cooler is mislabelled as a "tv" or "laptop", the food container is mislabelled as a "cup" in frame 2 and a "mouse" in frame 5, and the Reese's wrapper and foreground tray in frame 5 are missed entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints of the woman seated ~0.9–1.2 m directly in front of the camera wearer, showing her shoulders, upper torso, elbows, and crossed wrists resting on the table within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m) of the tabletop cup, bottle, and food items. Her shoulder line and facial keypoints (eyes, nose, and ears visible in frames 1–4) are oriented directly toward the camera wearer, with her head tilted slightly to her right in frame 1 before straightening and tilting slightly downward as the camera view pitches down across frames 2 to 4. Because the table occludes her lower body and the upper frame edge crops her head increasingly from frame 2 to frame 5, only her upper-body skeleton and a dense magenta cluster for her right hand resting over her left wrist are rendered. This map reveals the exact articulation of her crossed forearms, elbow angles, and right-hand finger joints against her dark maroon sweater, which blend together in the RGB frames. However, the pose map is completely unreliable in frame 5 where it fails to detect her body or hands at all once her head is fully cropped out of view, and in frames 1–4 where her partially occluded left hand lacks a magenta hand skeleton and a stray yellow lower-body keypoint appears near the bottom of frame 4.
